messages:
olga: heads up — ca-central1 apiserver watch streams started stalling ~09:12 UTC. correlation with a network MTU change from infra-net at ~09:10. seeing controller-manager leader churn and a surge in GPU node provisioning. cc @mike @sam

mike: logs? any packet loss or icmp fragments?

olga: paste logs:
```
May 10 09:12:33 kube-proxy[1234]: IF eth0 rx_errors=1245 dropped=1189 tx_errors=0
apiserver metrics: watch_count=12040 watch_streams_active=2820 watch_requeues=358
controller-manager: leader_changes=3 cpu_pct=112
```

sam: etcd 99p latency also spiked ~09:12 — looks like watch event delivery slowed, not full WAL issues.

carla: metric snippet from 09:05-09:30:
```
etcd_disk_commit_duration_seconds{quantile="0.99"} 0.81
apiserver_watch_stream_latency_seconds{p99} 0.95
```

ben: controller-manager started flapping leadership (3 flips in 6m). autoscaler saw controller-manager pod churn and interpreted it as capacity shortage — scaled GPU pool by +12 nodes. cost alarm triggered.

rachel: cost quick calc: ~12 x p4d-ish GPUs @ ~$3.2/hr each => ~38.4/hr => ~$921/day just from the new nodes (this is prox, will refine).

mike: immediate mitigations we can try: revert MTU at border, restart kube-proxy on affected nodes, increase apiserver keepalive/streaming timeouts to avoid premature requeues. Also consider temporarily raising controller-manager leader lease duration.

olga: rolled back MTU change at 09:28 UTC. packet-loss on kube-proxy dropped to ~0.2% from ~7% in 5m window.

devops-bot: action: rolling-restart job kube-proxy-target-ca-central1 started (job=kp-restart-4901)

carla: to stabilize leadership we patched controller-manager with a higher lease duration and ensured 3 replicas:
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy kube-controller-manager --replicas=3
kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy kube-controller-manager --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/command","value":["/usr/local/bin/kube-controller-manager","--leader-elect=true","--leader-elect-lease-duration=30s"]}]'
```

ben: disabled aggressive GPU scale-ups in the autoscaler policy and cordoned/drained the 6 most-recently-created gpu nodes to stop further spin-up.

rachel: updated cost estimate after cordon: transient hit ~+$520 for the incident window, not the full $921. still material — will tag spend to incident.

sam: monitoring shows watch_requeues falling to baseline by 09:40 after MTU rollback + kube-proxy restarts. controller-manager leader stable since 09:36.

olga: summary: root cause appears to be MTU reduction at network edge causing fragmentation/loss that disproportionately affected kube-proxy -> apiserver watch delivery, which cascaded to controller-manager flaps and then autoscaler overprovisioning GPUs.

mike: follow-ups: 1) add MTU change checklist (test on canary nodes + watch saturation sim), 2) add automated guardrail to pause cluster-autoscaler if control-plane leadership churn > 2 in 5m, 3) add network playbook note re conntrack tuning for small MTU environments.

rachel: I'll open a spend ticket and tag to incident-CA-4901234567.

olga: thanks everyone — closing thread but leaving a short postmortem action item list in #postmortems. please add any missing notes here. :thumbsup:
